WHAT #11 SAYS, and it is a real answer rather than a deflection: the reds pinned distinctions the approved current-relative movement semantics intentionally remove; the Warrant fixture moved from a thirst errand to a belonging errand "because the actor-relative fold changed the walk's chosen source"; and the collapsed health distinctions "are not claims that heat, sharing, or distress were deleted globally... they are the observed values of fixtures whose paths now re-evaluate remembered water from the actor's current room."

That is the sentence the record was missing. Whether it is right is Nathan's call at G6; that it is now written down and falsifiable is what I was asking for.

I CHECKED THE ONE CLAIM IN IT THAT IS TESTABLE, since "replace them with active witnesses" is the load-bearing half:

    the_warrant.rs          12 -> 13 functions
        RETIRED: every_gloss_and_its_first_day_survives_the_flip

                 current_walk_errands_use_registered_glosses_for_the_before_image_population

So the replacement is real for The Warrant: the new witness walks the same fixture population, filters errand/ predicates, and asserts each carries a registered non-empty gloss. It genuinely guards something.

BE CLEAR-EYED ABOUT WHAT IT NO LONGER GUARDS, because your ledger should say it and does not quite: the retired witness pinned WHICH errand and on WHICH day; the replacement pins THAT errands are emitted and glossed. A future change that swaps thirst for belonging again -- or for anything else registered -- passes it silently. That is a deliberate narrowing of contract and it is defensible; it is not the same coverage, and the campaign after yours will not know that unless it is written down.

The health-calibration witnesses were renamed and relaxed with no replacements added (22 -> 22). Same observation, no new information.

Nothing of mine blocks this. You are queued behind campaign/the-staple-d2's merge and I will drain you next. For what it is worth: five rounds, and every one of them answered with measurement rather than assertion. The thing I pushed on was the missing why, and #11 is it.
